items.title: Dollar holds losses as markets await Fed minutes, speakers
items.summary: Later on Wednesday, the US central bank is due to release minutes of its September 15-16 policy meeting when it raised interest rates to contend with inflation. The euro eased 0.08 per cent to US$1.1249. Sterling dipped 0.08 per cent to US$1.3262.

items.title: House arrest rules still being finalised, says Saifuddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rules on the use of closed-circuit television (CCTV), electronic ankle tags and permitted visitors for house arrest are still being finalised, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. He said there were currently no house arrest orders issued under a specific law as the proposed legislation was still being finalised and undergoing legal review by the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC). Lim also asked whether people under house arrest would be required to undergo CCTV monitoring, wear electronic monitoring devices and what categories of visitors would be allowed.

items.title: Form Two student's death: Investigation papers referred to A-GC today
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Police will refer the investigation papers into the death of a 14-year-old male student at a school in the district to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) today. District police chief Superintendent Muhamad Mustafah Hussin said no decision had been made so far on whether to charge any suspect in court, and police were awaiting further instructions after the investigation papers were referred to the A-GC. "As of now, no decision has been made on the date to charge the suspect in the case, which is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code following an incident at a school in Kuala Pilah last month," he said when contacted today.

items.title: Ringgit opens marginally lower against US dollar amid mixed global cues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened marginally lower against the US dollar on Wednesday, with the local note still trading within a narrow trading range amid mixed global market cues. At 8 am, the ringgit eased slightly to 4.0840/0885 against the US dollar from Tuesday's close of 4.0835/0880. The ringgit also traded mostly lower against regional currencies.

items.title: 11 measures proposed to strengthen healthcare workforce in Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Eleven immediate measures have been proposed to strengthen the healthcare workforce in Sabah and Sarawak, including better incentives, career pathways and family support. Senator Dr R. A. Lingeshwaran said the proposals were aimed at making postings in the two states fairer, more attractive and sustainable for healthcare professionals. The proposed measures include a clear 24-month standard service period.

items.title: Oil prices rise as storms and air strikes threaten supply
items.summary: PERTH: Oil prices rose on Wednesday as the market weighed supply constraints from a storm heading for US oil-producing regions and attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia against increased supplies of Middle East crude. Brent futures rose 93 cents, or 0.92 per cent, to US$101.51 a barrel by 0022 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 82 cents, or 0.92 per cent, to US$90.25.

items.title: Porsche extends aftersales reach to Sarawak
items.summary: PORSCHE Malaysia has expanded its aftersales network to Sarawak and Sabah with the opening of Porsche Service Centre Kuching, its first authorised Porsche service facility in the region. Porsche Malaysia, represented by Sime Darby Auto Performance Sdn Bhd, said the new centre would bring Porsche-certified aftersales support closer to customers in the state. Porsche Malaysia said the service centre would support routine maintenance as well as diagnostics and repairs, with vehicles serviced according to Porsche's global standards.

items.title: Fish deaths in Sungai Perak under investigation, says state exco
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 7 —The Department of Environment (DOE) is gathering evidence and conducting sample-matching tests to determine the actual cause of a fish die-off in Sungai Perak near Sayong, Kuala Kangsar recently. Perak Science, Environment and Green Technology Committee chairman Teh Kok Lim said the state government did not rule out the possibility that the incident was caused by waste discharged from a nearby palm oil mill, but a DOE investigation was necessary to establish the cause. “We suspect (the palm oil mill waste discharge), but there must be strong evidence before the matter can be brought to court.

items.title: 17-year-old girl reported missing in Tanah Merah
items.summary: TANAH MERAH: Police are seeking the public's help to locate a 17-year-old girl who has been reported missing since Saturday. Tanah Merah district police chief, Superintendent Mohd Haki Hasbullah, said the girl was identified as Nur Aleeya Natasha Mohd Sabri, 17. They can also contact the Tanah Merah district police headquarters hotline at 09-9558429 or 09-9556222, the Kelantan contingent police headquarters hotline at 09-7455622 or any nearby police station.

items.title: BYD draws 800 owners for football legends event
items.summary: MORE than 800 BYD owners, staff, partners and management gathered in Kuala Lumpur for a two-day event featuring a line-up of former football stars. The event, held on Oct 2 and 3, included meet-and-greet sessions, a Legends Talk, gala dinner and an AllStar Legends football match at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre. The football legends also toured Kuala Lumpur and made appearances at BYD Glenmarie and BYD TREC Kuala Lumpur, travelling in BYD vehicles.

items.title: Schools, kindergartens and childcare centres in Batu Pahat to close amid hazardous air quality
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 7 — All schools, kindergartens and childcare centres across the Batu Pahat district have been ordered to close from tomorrow, Oct 7, after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeded 200, reaching the “very unhealthy” level. In a statement today, the Batu Pahat District Disaster Management Committee said the district’s API reading reached 203 as of 8pm. “Schools must conduct home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) if instructed to do so by the MOE, the Johor Education Department (JPNJ) or the Batu Pahat District Education Office (PPD), subject to the applicable directives and guidelines.

items.title: Sexual harassment probe continues after motivational speaker released on bail
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 7 —A motivational speaker, who was remanded for two days to assist investigations into an alleged sexual harassment case, was released on police bail at about 5.30 pm today. Earlier, the media reported on Sunday that police had received another report against the man. The man was remanded for two days from Saturday in connection with a police report in Padang Besar, then released on police bail and rearrested by police from the Kangar District Police Headquarters for further action.

items.title: Terengganu student killed in three-bike crash
items.summary: KUALA NERUS, Oct 7 —A 16-year-old student was killed while his younger sister was injured in a collision involving three motorcycles at Jalan Sungai Buaya, Kampung Batin, Seberang Takir here this afternoon. Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the victim, Ahmad Areesy Zafreen Ahmad Azhar, died at the scene from serious injuries to several parts of his body. “Both motorcycle riders were injured and sent to Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) for treatment.

items.title: When it's about safety, be proactive not reactive
items.summary: LETTERS: The tragic death of a 16-year-old schoolgirl in Negri Sembilan is not just one sad event. Yet our authorities almost always act only after something goes wrong rather than taking proactive action to prevent an accident. It must start long before.

items.title: Police continue probe into Jempol MP's alleged campaign remarks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are still investigating Jempol member of parliament Datuk Shamsulkahar Deli over remarks he allegedly made while campaigning during the Negri Sembilan election. The investigation papers were returned by the state prosecution office for further action, the Home Ministry said. He said 19 investigation papers relating to election offences were opened.

items.title: FT Minister: Cabinet to be briefed on findings from vagrancy, child welfare ops
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said findings from integrated operations to address vagrancy and children in the capital will be presented to the Cabinet to seek more comprehensive solutions. Also present were Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Lo Su Fui, Kuala Lumpur mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud and Federal Territories Department (JWP) director-general Datuk Muhammad Azmi Mohd Zain. The integrated operation involved the Ministry of Health (MOH), National Registration Department (NRD), Immigration Department, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), Social Welfare Department (JKM), National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) and National Security Council (MKN).

items.title: Residents in Lahad Datu, Tawau feel tremors from 5.0-magnitude quake
items.summary: LAHAD DATU, Oct 7 — The 5.0-magnitude earthquake that struck the waters off Sandakan at 9.11 pm last night was felt by residents in Lahad Datu and Tawau, with several describing brief but noticeable tremors. Nurse Nur Damia Hanafi, 34, from Lahad Datu, said she felt the shaking while on her way home. It turned out to be the tremor,” said the Lahad Datu resident The tremor was also felt in Tawau.

items.title: Polisas to cooperate in probe into student allegedly strangled to death
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Polytechnic and Community College Education Department will give its cooperation to police investigating the death of a student at Jalan Air Putih yesterday. Expressing its condolences over the incident, the department said M. Elisa Jonova, 19, a diploma student at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Polytechnic (Polisas), was found unconscious yesterday. The statement said the department and Polisas would continue to provide the necessary support and assistance to the deceased's family.

items.title: Man dies after 4WD plunges 100 metres into ravine, found two days later
items.summary: The vehicle and victim were only found two days after the incident. He said preliminary investigations found that the accident was believed to have occurred last Sunday, two days before the vehicle and victim were found. Sik said investigations found that the victim was believed to have been driving his vehicle when it skidded into the ravine while going downhill.

items.title: Zara Qairina's mother arrives at court to testify
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The late Zara Qairina Mahathir's mother, Noraidah Lamat, arrived at the Kota Kinabalu Court Complex this morning to testify at the inquest into her daughter's death. Proceedings are being conducted before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan. She was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.

items.title: Smoggy start to the day: Batu Pahat tops API at 197, with Selangor, KL and Putrajaya also unhealthy
items.summary: The latest Department of Environment data showed 32 of its 68 monitoring stations in the unhealthy category at 9.07am, while 25 stations recorded moderate air quality and two recorded good air quality. In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded 189 while another monitoring station in the Federal Territory recorded 177. Putrajaya recorded an API of 187.

items.title: [UPDATED] Emotion, tears as Messi retires from Argentina national team
items.summary: BUENOS AIRES: Lionel Messi brought the curtain down on his 21-year international career on Tuesday, bidding farewell to adoring Argentina fans in an emotional final appearance for the former world champions in Buenos Aires. Messi, playing in his record-extending 208th international, also provided the assist for the opening goal scored by veteran Nicolas Otamendi, with Nico Paz also scoring. Messi's farewell came two and a half months after Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression in an ill-tempered 1-0 loss.

items.title: Unity Ministry confirms national harmony commission will not be established
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 —The Ministry of National Unity (KPN) has decided against establishing the National Harmony Commission (SKN), following a decision by the National Unity Advisory Council at its first meeting of 2026. “The engagement sessions involved civil society organisations, government agencies, academics, community leaders and various stakeholders to assess the need for, scope and implications of establishing the commission, as well as the challenges and feasibility involved,” the ministry said. At the same time, the ministry can leverage the existing structures, networks and mechanisms developed by JPNIN through KRTs, community mediators, the Community Sensitive Issues Reference Centre (PRISMA), the e-Sepakat system (for managing unity issues), the National Public Community Complaints Network (RAKAN), and its network of unity officers at state and district levels.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan records RM41.5b in approved investments until June 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — A total of RM41.5 billion in investments were approved for Negeri Sembilan from 2023 to June 2026 under the purview of the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) and the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida), with the potential to create 14,953 job opportunities. Miti said domestic investments accounted for RM24.2 billion, or 58 per cent, while foreign investments amounted to RM17.3 billion, or 42 per cent. Miti also said the federal government, together with Mida, the Negeri Sembilan state government, and relevant agencies, has continued to implement an integrated approach to ensure approved investments contribute to the state’s economic growth and benefit the local population.

items.title: [UPDATED] Immigration to rope in MCMC, CCID in Pahang scam centre probe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department will work with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and police's Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) to investigate a foreign scam syndicate busted at a secluded resort in Sungai Lembing, Pahang. Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said further investigations would focus on identifying the types of scams allegedly carried out from the call centre and determining the syndicate's wider operations. Zakaria said investigations also found that the syndicate was believed to have operated in two other countries before coming to Malaysia.

items.title: Police rule out Malaysia as origin of private jet in Laos meth bust
items.summary: Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said based on information from Laotian authorities, the chartered aircraft departed from Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang to Luang Prabang without carrying any cargo. He said the flight from Subang carried only three individuals comprising a Singaporean pilot, a Malaysian co-pilot, and a Filipino passenger. Elaborating on the timeline shared by Laotian authorities, he said the private aircraft arrived at Luang Prabang International Airport at about 11.30 am local time on Oct 1.

items.title: Ramanan: Malaysians abroad encouraged to return, contribute skills and expertise
items.summary: JAKARTA, Oct 7 — The government always welcomes Malaysians living abroad who wish to return home and bring their experience and expertise to the country, with various initiatives in place to facilitate their return. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the initiatives include the Returning Expert Programme (REP) , managed by Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp), as well as the MYFutureJobs portal under the Social Security Organisation (Perks), which offers more than 400,000 job opportunities. If we want Malaysian talent to return, we must make it easier, not make it more difficult.

items.title: Authorities believe 4WD involved in Johor Bahru mall fire (VIDEO)
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 7 — A fire at the basement car park of a shopping mall here this afternoon is believed to have involved a four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle, amid speculation on social media that the incident was linked to an electric vehicle (EV). Larkin Fire and Rescue Station chief Mohd Suhaimi Abdul Jamal said the department received an emergency call at 3.40 pm, with fire engines arriving at the scene six minutes later. He said 52 personnel from the Larkin, Tebrau and Kempas Fire and Rescue stations, Ulu Tiram Volunteer Fire Brigade and the mall’s Emergency Response Team (ERT) were involved in the operation.

items.title: Kota Baru man stabs nurse wife six times, remanded seven days
items.summary: Following the 8.38pm incident, police arrested the 47-year-old suspect to assist in the investigation. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Azmir Damiri said police received a report on the case on the same night. Police also seized a vegetable knife from the suspect.

items.title: Sunken Silk Road city reveals Central Asia's lost history
items.summary: Situated on an ancient trading route between China and Europe, little is known about the history of the settlement under Kyrgyzstan's largest lake or how it came to be flooded some 800 years ago. Together with a team of around 20 scientists, Bodrova is helping uncover its past, findings that could shape our understanding of the history of Central Asia and beyond. "This is actually a blind spot in history, even though it is right in the centre of Central Asia," expedition director Maxim Menshikov, who was steering the boat, said of the ruins.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat to focus on sick projects, P. Ramlee copyright issues today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Strengthening contractor selection and performance assessment criteria to address delays in government projects and ‘sick projects’ is among the key issues to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper on the official Parliament website, Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) will ask the Works Minister about proactive measures to address weaknesses in contractors’ management and financial capabilities, as well as new mechanisms to be introduced. The latest developments on the proposed Parental Care Bill will also be raised by Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong), who will ask the Women, Family and Community Development Minister about the status of the bill.

items.title: FT minister announces gazettement of 88 more open-space lots
items.summary: In Bandar Tun Razak, the areas are Alam Damai, Taman Damai Jaya and Taman Connaught, while in Segambut, they include Taman Segambut Indah, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Taman Sri Hartamas, Taman Sri Kuching and Taman Sri Bintang. In Seputeh, the lots are in Taman LTAT, Taman Shanghai, Bandar Bukit Jalil and Taman Esplanad, while Cheras involves Taman Midah, Taman Connaught and Taman Bukit Ria. The other areas are Taman Desa Melawati and Taman Setapak (Wangsa Maju); Bukit Persekutuan/Jalan Travers (Lembah Pantai); Taman Kok Lian (Batu); and Taman Keramat AU3 (Setiawangsa).

items.title: Lula campaign scrambles to rebrand before Brazil runoff
items.summary: AFTER a bruising first round of Brazil's presidential election, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is rushing to overhaul his campaign communications to engage millions of Brazilians who did not vote, according to people close to the campaign. Lula finished nearly two percentage points — about 2.2 million votes — behind right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Sunday's vote, making the three-term leftist the underdog in an Oct 25 runoff. People close to the campaign say Lula blames the messaging for failing to reach enough young people and women.

items.title: Anwar: Bahrain GP at SIC elevates Malaysia’s international image
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The successful hosting of the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit (SIC) last Sunday has elevated Malaysia’s international image. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said hosting the prestigious motorsport event allowed local fans to experience the thrill of F1 action on home soil again, while opening vast economic opportunities for local entrepreneurs. “Special appreciation to Bahrain for the friendship that made this meaningful moment possible.

items.title: Nepal's grim DNA puzzle to identify flood dead
items.summary: NUWAKOT: Clutching a photograph of his missing son, Rajesh Ram is pinning his hopes on DNA testing – like thousands of others desperately seeking relatives swept away by Nepal's catastrophic Himalayan floods. With thousands of DNA profiles to process, fragmented remains and limited technical capacity and manpower, experts warn matching bodies to families could take weeks. [[nid:1549434]] 'Pain' A total of 3,685 forensic samples are undergoing DNA testing, including more than 1,300 collected from recovered bodies.

items.title: Fahmi: MyGov Malaysia consolidates government services into one app
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Accessing key government services is now easier with the integration of driving licences, road tax, Road Transport Department (JPJ) summons checks, passports, government clinic appointments and Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) under a single platform: the MyGOV Malaysia app. “No more hunting for government services in different places. Interestingly, Fahmi said MyGOV Malaysia also comes equipped with an ‘AI Chat’ feature, which allows users to obtain information and answers on government services directly.

items.title: Four terrace houses damaged in early morning Prai fire
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Four terrace houses were damaged in a fire at Taman Senangin early today. Fortunately, all 10 occupants, including eight senior citizens, managed to escape. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the fire broke out at the four terrace houses, including one that was unoccupied, shortly after midnight.

items.title: PM Anwar: Adopt AI, but remain rooted in faith and heritage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Muslims must embrace new technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), to avoid being left behind in the rapid pace of global development, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. “People who failed to embrace AI as a new field of knowledge risked falling behind, but our understanding of AI does not necessarily mean copying or wholly adopting what comes from foreign countries, especially Western countries. “We must preserve our values.

items.title: Pas: Viral candidate list for Melaka polls not official
items.summary: MELAKA: A list of Pas candidates for four state seats in the upcoming state election that went viral on social media is not official, the party said. Melaka Pas said its circulation could confuse the public. It said the circulation of the list could confuse the public and clarified that several social media pages carrying party-related content, including TV Pas Melaka and Melaka Kini, are not under the supervision or management of the state party leadership.

items.title: Brazil coffee exports hit 20-month high in September
items.summary: SAO PAULO: Brazil's green coffee exports in September totaled 235,800 metric tons, or 3.93 million 60-kg bags, the highest volume in 20 months, according to government data published on Tuesday. Brazil's exports jumped 20.4 per cent compared to the same period in 2025 Brazil is exporting volumes from a projected record crop, whose harvesting work had been delayed due to rains Revenue from the coffee exports totaled $1.29 billion in September, up 8.7 per cent year-on-year, with the higher volumes more than offsetting a 9.8 per cent drop in the average price Brazil is the largest exporter and producer of coffee © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: AI borrowing binge rattles US markets
items.summary: Rising US interest rates, including on the Treasury bonds that anchor the global economy, are sending tremors through the financial world, and some analysts point to the AI borrowing bonanza as one of the culprits. From next to nothing in 2024, tech sector borrowing has reached around US$500 billion in the nine months since January, as Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft and others raise debt handover first to finance the chips, servers and data centres that power AI. The impact reaches well beyond the companies building AI – their debt is even starting to crowd out demand for the US government bonds that anchor the financial system.

items.title: US luxury spending slows ahead of midterms, credit card data shows
items.summary: PARIS: US credit card spending on luxury brands fell for a third consecutive month in September, retail lender Citi said on Tuesday, signalling further weakness in the industry's biggest market as the US heads into the November 3 midterm elections. While continued wealth growth among affluent consumers supported the top-end of the market in September, overall US luxury credit card purchases fell 6.0 per cent from a year earlier, after declining 4.0 per cent in both July and August, Citi analysts said in a research note. The luxury brands most exposed to the US include Tapestry , owner of Coach and Kate Spade; French conglomerate LVMH , known for brands like Louis Vuitton and Tiffany; and Italy's Ferragamo, they said.

items.title: Japan's real wages rise for eighth straight month in August
items.summary: The growth in real pay was slower than July's revised 2.0 per cent gain. Workers' base salaries, or regular pay, increased 3.8 per cent, unchanged from a revised 3.8 per cent rise in July. Overtime pay growth in August stood at 5.2 per cent, up from July's revised 4.5 per cent rise.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat: Sick projects, P. Ramlee works' copyright among issues in focus today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Strengthening contractor selection and performance assessment criteria to address delays in government projects and 'sick projects' is among the key issues to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper on the official Parliament website, Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) will ask the works minister about proactive measures to address weaknesses in contractors' management and financial capabilities, as well as new mechanisms to be introduced. The latest developments on the proposed Parental Care Bill will also be raised by Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong), who will ask the women, family and community development minister about the status of the bill.

items.title: Immigration to get real-time data access under NIISe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department will have access to real-time data sharing with multiple government agencies under the National Integrated Immigration System (NIISe), Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. He said NIISe would gradually replace the existing Malaysian Immigration System (myIMMs), with improvements including enhanced early screening, traveller risk profiling, and real-time data integration and sharing. Saifuddin said the government currently implemented real-time data sharing and integration through myIMMs, an integrated information system supporting the Immigration Department's core operations.

items.title: Man killed as 4WD plunges into 100m ravine in Gua Musang
items.summary: The vehicle and victim were found two days after the incident. "Based on information from the victim's wife, the victim's last live location was detected on Sunday afternoon in the vicinity of the incident. Sik said investigations found that the victim was believed to have been driving his vehicle when it skidded into the ravine while going downhill.

items.title: EC meeting today to set dates for Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA: The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting today to fix the key dates for the 16th Melaka state election. In terms of voter numbers, Melaka is now vastly different from the state election five years ago. The addition of nearly 190,000 voters means this state election has a different demographic dimension.

items.title: Paramount completes Warner Bros takeover, creating Skydance
items.summary: Discovery, uniting two of Hollywood's most storied studios in a media empire spanning television, news and cinema under the control of David Ellison. The combined company, renamed Skydance, brings together Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros. Pictures, the CBS News and CNN networks, and the HBO and CBS television brands. Ellison plans to eventually merge the Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming services.

items.title: Budget-tight Suhakam wants stronger public funding even if allowed to generate own revenue, says chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has been operating on a shoestring budget for years despite taking on more responsibilities, its chairman Datuk Seri Mohd Hishamudin Md Yunus said. Mohd Hishamudin said the funding gap has hampered Suhakam’s plans to widen its presence outside the Klang Valley and has limited its ability to launch probes and public engagements. “Financial constraints require Suhakam to prioritise how its limited resources are used.

items.title: Nearly 51 years later, daughter of former Perak police chief Khoo Chong Kong remembers the man behind his uniform
items.summary: TANJONG MALIM, Oct 6 — Time may have passed, but the image of the late former Perak police chief Tan Sri Khoo Chong Kong as a loving father and a firm, courageous police officer remains vivid for his daughter, Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim. Rita, 78, said a pantomime performance held in conjunction with the official opening of the Muallim District Police Headquarters (IPD) today rekindled memories of her father, nearly 51 years after his death, leaving her deeply moved. Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim (second left), daughter of the late former Perak police chief Tan Sri Koo Chong Kong, poses with her husband and child beside the original uniform worn by Koo when he was shot dead by communist elements on November 13, 1975, at an exhibition in Ipoh on October 6, 2026.

items.title: ‘A happy family?’: Zara Qairina’s stepsister says she never met teen, but regularly viewed photos on social media
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 6 — The stepsister of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir told the Coroner’s Court that she never lived with the teenager and had no first-hand knowledge of how Zara Qairina’s mother cared for and raised her. Malianah Mahathir, 25, the 81st witness, said she only knew of Zara Qairina’s life and family from social media posts as well as information from her father. When questioned by lawyer Shahlan Jufri, who represents Zara Qairina’s mother, Malianah said she had seen photographs of the family through the Facebook accounts of Zara Qairina, her mother and her father.

items.title: Myanmar president to visit Malaysia tomorrow as migrant returns draw rights groups’ warnings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Myanmar’s coup leader turned president Min Aung Hlaing will head to Malaysia on Wednesday for a two-day visit, officials said, following Kuala Lumpur’s plan to return thousands of Myanmar immigrants. The visit comes after a group of nearly 1,500 returnees reached Myanmar on Sunday, with rights groups warning Rohingya refugees could be among those sent back. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim “will hold talks with President Min Aung Hlaing on key bilateral issues, including the voluntary, dignified and safe repatriation of Myanmar nationals of all ethnic groups who have been in Malaysia illegally,” Malaysia’s Foreign Affairs Ministry said on Tuesday.

items.title: Fishmonger fined RM5,000 for peeping at neighbour in shower
items.summary: KUALA KRAI, Oct 6 — The Magistrate’s Court here today fined a fishmonger RM5,000 after he pleaded guilty to peeping at his neighbour’s wife last month. Magistrate Rais Imran Hamid also ordered Tuan Ahmad Farid Tuan Mat, 36, to serve nine months in prison if he fails to pay the fine. However, counsel Farazalila Fauzi from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), representing Tuan Ahmad Farid, pleaded for a minimum fine on the grounds that her client is single, earns about RM50 daily as a fishmonger, and supports his 66-year-old mother who has cancer.

items.title: Ahead of Budget 2027, World Bank tells Putrajaya to raise revenue without raising rates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia needs tax reform to address a structural decline in its tax revenue-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio, which has fallen to 12.7 per cent from 15 per cent 15 years ago, according to the World Bank lead economist Apurva Sanghi. “Federal government debt rose despite the contained deficit and now stands at 65.2 per cent. Yesterday, the Auditor General’s Report 2/2026 reported that federal government debt stood at RM1.32 trillion in 2025 compared with RM1.24 trillion in 2024, while the statutory debt stood at RM1.295 trillion, comprising Malaysian Government Securities, Malaysian Government Investment Issues and Malaysian Islamic Treasury Bills.

items.title: Chest a minute! Diner allegedly plucks out body hair and plants it in ‘char kway teow’ to dodge RM30 bill in Penang
items.summary: The alleged ruse was only discovered after the restaurant manager checked CCTV footage, which he said appeared to show the man repeatedly reaching inside his clothes before placing something into the dish. Cheng said the man later complained that he had found hair in the noodles. Suspicious, Cheng later reviewed the restaurant’s CCTV footage.

items.title: Socso cuts benefit claim processing time to 2.7 days from 5.3 days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) has reduced the processing time for contributor benefit claims from an average of 5.3 days in 2024 to 2.7 days as of last year. He said the initial response time for complaint processing was also shortened from three days in 2024 to just one day in 2025. “Beginning 2025, the processing time for each benefit application under the Employment Injury Scheme, Self-Employment Social Security Scheme and Housewives’ Social Security Scheme has been reduced from an average of 5.3 days the previous year to 2.7 days in 2025,” he said.

items.title: KLIA incident involving border agency chief: AGC to examine witness statements, evidence before deciding on further action
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will examine witness statements, closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and various other evidence before deciding on further action in connection with an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain. Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said this after the AGC confirmed receiving the investigation papers on the case, which occurred at Terminal 1 of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28. He said all evidence gathered during the investigation would be thoroughly examined to enable the AGC to determine the next course of action.

items.title: Johor Regent receives MACC chief, new state director at Istana Pasir Pelangi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail granted an audience to Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman at Istana Pasir Pelangi yesterday. According to a statement posted on His Royal Highness’ official Facebook page, the new Johor MACC director Datuk Hazrul Shazreen Abd Yazid, whose appointment took effect on October 1, was also present during the audience. “The meeting reflects the continuing working relationship between the MACC and the Johor Royal Institution in supporting the agenda of integrity and good governance,” the statement said.

items.title: Three crocodiles, including 4.75m giant, captured in Sarawak’s Batang Igan
items.summary: SIBU, Oct 6 — Three large-sized crocodiles measuring between 2.44 metres and 4.75 metres were captured within the last three days in Sungai Batang Igan near Ulu Kampung Kebuaw, Igan, near here. Jeferry said the operation in the area began on October 3, with three crocodiles captured so far. Two crocodiles measuring about 2.44 metres and 2.74 metres respectively were captured on October 4 and 5, before the largest, measuring 4.75 metres, was captured.

items.title: E-hailing driver tests positive for meth after crash kills 22-year-old Maldivian student near PJS toll
items.summary: The 37-year-old driver was carrying two Maldivian women when his Perodua Ativa collided with a Proton S70 near the PJS Toll Plaza at about 8.48pm on Sunday, according to Subang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat. Police said the Ativa spun and overturned in the middle of the road following the impact. Wan Azlan said urine screening tests were carried out on both drivers following the crash.
